title: Ariadne saga diagram
description: A saga state machine as an Ariadne diagram (format version 3, see docs/specs/diagram-format.md). Files of versions 1 and 2 are still read by Ariadne, but only the current version is described here. Rules that need to look across the file (unique ids, edges that point at existing nodes, one `any` node) are checked by Ariadne itself, not by this schema.

name.description: Title of the saga, e.g. `Order Saga`. Exports use it as the title.

description.description: What the saga does; shown under the title in exports.

saga.description: What generating or importing C# needs to know about the saga. All optional.

namespace.description: Namespace of the state machine and the saga instance, e.g. `Shop.Orders`.

stateProperty.description: The instance property holding the current state, e.g. `CurrentState`.

contractsNamespace.description: Namespace of the message contracts (commands and events), when not the saga's.

source.description: The C# file that implements the saga, relative to this file, with `/` as separator, e.g. `../Sagas/OrderStateMachine.cs`.

events.description: What is known in code about an event, one entry per event. An event no entry describes is implicit (message type = name, correlated by `CorrelationId`).

name.description: The event, as transitions name it. Unique in the list.

messageType.description: The message type, when it is not called like the event, e.g. `SubmitOrder`.

correlation.description: `CorrelationId`, or the correlation as written in code, e.g. `CorrelateById(context => context.Message.OrderId)`.

direction.description: Which way the flow runs, from the initial state on. Defaults to top-bottom.

spacing.description: Room between states and between layers. Defaults to normal (and is then left out).

nodes.description: The states. Ids are unique in the file; there is at most one `any` node.

edges.description: The transitions. Every `source` and `target` is the id of a node.

type.description: `start`: the initial state (nothing enters it). `state`: a state. `end`: a final state (nothing leaves it). `any`: transitions leaving it apply in every state; nothing enters it. `join`: waits until the events of all incoming transitions have arrived.

color.description: Accent color of the card: a palette name or a `#rrggbb` value.

activities.description: What the saga does on entering this state, in order. Only on `state` nodes.

command.description: Send a command to exactly one consumer, e.g. `ChargePayment`.

event.description: Publish an event to all subscribers, e.g. `OrderAccepted`.

ignores.description: Events the state receives and drops (`Ignore(E)`). Only on `state` nodes.

requests.description: Requests the state makes on entry. The answers are the events `<Name>.Completed`, `<Name>.Faulted` and `<Name>.TimeoutExpired`. Only on `state` nodes.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the reply, e.g. `30s`.

routingSlips.description: Routing slips the state starts on entry (ADR 0023). The outcomes are the events `<Name>.Completed` and `<Name>.Faulted`. Only on `state` nodes.

activities.description: The itinerary: the activities in the order they run.

compensates.description: It is undone (compensated) when a later activity faults.

timers.description: Timeouts the state schedules or cancels on entry, in order. Only on `state` nodes.

schedule.description: Schedule a timeout; when it fires the saga receives it as an event of this name.

delay.description: Only with `schedule`: how long until it fires, e.g. `30s`.

retry.description: Free text, e.g. `3 attempts`. Documentation only.

compensation.description: Undo action for the work done to reach this state.

source.description: Id of the state the saga is in.

target.description: Id of the state the transition enters.

kind.description: Compensation transitions are not laid out.

event.description: The event that triggers the transition, e.g. `PaymentCharged`.

eventSource.description: Where an external event comes from, e.g. `Shop API`.

guard.description: Condition for taking the transition, e.g. `amount > 100`. Needs an `event`.
